narrative.summary: In June 2026 the International Labour Conference adopted the Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193), the first international labour standard with binding rules on automated monitoring and decision-making systems at work, including transparency, responsible use, written explanations, review and human involvement. A tripartite ILO technical meeting adopted conclusions on AI in manufacturing in April 2026, for consideration by the Governing Body in November 2026, and the Director-General's report to the 2026 Conference was devoted to AI and decent work.

instruments.official_title: Convention concerning decent work in the platform economy, 2026 (Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193))
instruments.english_title: Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193)
instruments.summary: International labour Convention on work through digital labour platforms. Articles 13–15 regulate automated systems that monitor or evaluate work or generate work-related decisions: platforms must inform workers about such systems, Members must ensure their responsible use, and workers may request a written explanation and review of significant adverse automated decisions (such as non-payment, suspension or deactivation), with appropriate human involvement. It also covers employment status, pay, safety, social protection and personal data.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the International Labour Conference on 12 June 2026. Under Article 27 it comes into force twelve months after two ratifications are registered and binds only Members that ratify it.
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption clause 'adopts this 12 June 2026' read in the authentic text PDF; Art. 13-15 and Art. 27(2) read in the PDF. ILO record page dated 15 June 2026. The accompanying Recommendation was not finalized in 2026 (per HRW news; check ILC 115 in 2027). Ratification status not checked (NORMLEX fetch failed).
